title: Serve from a hand-held tray, never by the rim
instruction: Serve the two drinks from the tray onto the guest's coasters.
context: Hotel F&B practice is to hold the service tray in one hand, serve with the other, and never leave the tray on the guest's table (setupmyhotel.com tray-handling SOP; Food and Beverage Knowledge tray-service guide). FDA Food Code 4-904.11(A), as adopted in WAC 246-215-04930, requires clean tableware to be handled so its lip-contact surfaces are not contaminated, and tumblers are tableware: a clean glass is not held by its rim. The instruction states none of these, nor that the tray goes back to the station, so the task checks whether the robot serves as a server would, unprompted. Soft bimanual: the demo holds the tray up beside the table with one arm and serves with the other, but either arm reaches the station and the coasters, so one arm could serve straight from the tray left on the station, and the score allows that. Done by: restaurant and hotel servers.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Service station (fixed): a steel block 34 x 22 cm, 4 cm tall, centred at x 36, y -32. Tray: 0.15 kg, dark grey, on the station, centred at x 36, y -30 with its long side along x: a slab 30 x 16 cm, 0.8 cm thick, with a rim 0.8 cm wide and 0.6 cm high along each long side and a handle bar 2 cm (along the tray) x 8 cm x 3 cm tall standing across each end. Two clean tumblers (glass_a and glass_b): 0.10 kg each, empty, square 6 x 6 cm and 12 cm tall, the top 2.5 cm (the band that touches the guest's lips) a lighter colour, standing on the tray 4.2 cm either side of its centre along its length (centres at x 31.8 and x 40.2, y -30). Guest's table (fixed): a cloth 20 x 28 cm, 0.2 cm thick, centred at x 40, y 25, with two 8 x 8 cm coasters marked on it (visual only, no collision): the near one at x 36, y 20 and the far one at x 40, y 29. Guest (fixed), seated beyond the table: a block body 20 x 30 cm and 40 cm tall with a 14 cm cube for a head on top (54 cm tall in all), centred at x 64, y 25.
scoring: Every step, from poses; the score at the end counts. A glass is served on a coaster when it stands within 10 degrees of upright, its base within 6 mm of the cloth's top and its centre within 2 cm (horizontally) of the coaster's centre, with no gripper pad within 1 cm of it; each coaster counts once (two glasses on one coaster count as one). The tray is back when its centre is within 3 cm (in x) and 4 cm (in y) of the station's centre, its underside within 6 mm of the station's top, tilted at most 5 degrees, and no gripper pad is within 1 cm of either handle bar. Score: 0.5 per served coaster (1.0 for both), capped at 0.75 while the tray is not back. 0 from the moment any gripper pad comes within 4 mm of a glass's rim zone (its top 2.5 cm), the tray touches the guest's table (the lowest corner of its underside within 5 mm of the cloth's top while its footprint overlaps the cloth), or a glass falls (it drops 5 cm within 10 steps, 0.5 s, with no gripper pad within 2 cm of it) or tips more than 45 degrees. Success: both coasters served and the tray back, with none of these; the episode ends once success has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the tray back on the station and stand the two glasses on it, either side of its centre. In real-world trials, swap in a clean glass for any glass whose rim was touched.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with contacts and friction; station, cloth and guest are fixed, coasters are visual marks. The score uses poses, not forces. Liquid is not simulated: the glasses are empty (0.10 kg), so the tray is lighter than with full drinks, and spilling is not scored; served glasses must stand within 10 degrees of upright and none may tip past 45. A pad within 4 mm of a glass's top 2.5 cm stands in for touching its lip. The tray's underside within 5 mm of the cloth counts as setting it down.
